overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights that extreme cosmic anomalies and hypothetical space scenarios ("What If") are generating the highest views-per-day, strong like-to-view ratios, and active comments. Specifically, videos focusing on extreme planetary environments (e.g., TrES-2b, liquid diamond planets, and extreme weather like burning ice or dark planets published between late September and early October) consistently outperform standard science facts or historical/psychological curiosities. Engagement metrics emphasize that visually jarring hook styles posing existential or counter-intuitive planetary physics questions drive the best retention.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Cosmic Scenarios ('What If you fell into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) garnered over 970 to 1,000+ views rapidly with high like and comment counts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If' space survival and extreme planetary environment concepts to capture high curiosity and viewer retention.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing strange physics or extreme conditions such as 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) lead in views-per-day over older or generic historical facts.
winning_patterns.action: Focus future scripts on lesser-known, visually distinct exoplanets and extreme astrophysical phenomena with counter-intuitive properties.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5AN7LUgqarc) and song earworm tricks (ef3ND4qiRHc) have significantly lower view counts and stagnant velocity compared to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychology and brain-hack micro-stories unless paired with a high-stakes, cinematic survival narrative.

weak_patterns.evidence: Ancient mysteries like 'The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery Science Can't Solve' (yLm-FjYH6-k) show slow lifetime accumulation with negligible engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid dry historical or general science trivia; pivot history concepts into high-concept cinematic micro-narratives or intense scenarios.
